summary: The note surveys the growth of eco-art festivals worldwide since the early 21st century, tracing the movement to 1960s-70s land art and rising climate awareness. It walks through festivals held from September to November 2023 in cities including Portland, Asheville, Chicago, London, Santa Fe, Seattle and New York, highlighting community involvement, youth participation, new sustainable techniques and indigenous artists. It concludes that these festivals foster an environmentally conscious culture and have lasting impacts through grants and education.
one_line: Overview of eco-art festivals in 2023 that merge artistic creativity with sustainability, community engagement, indigenous wisdom and innovative eco-friendly techniques.
key_facts: The eco-art movement's roots trace to the conceptual and land art traditions of the 1960s and 1970s, while the current wave is credited to growing public awareness of climate change.
Patricia Johanson, John Dahlsen, and Olafur Eliasson are named as artists who bridged environmental causes and artistic expression.

The 'Green Canvas Festival' was held on September 5, 2023, in Portland, Oregon, and was founded by curator Stella Marquez; it featured interactive installations, recycled sculptures and workshops on organic art materials.

Environmental scientist Emily Raine gave a keynote at California's 'Harmony with Nature' art symposium on September 12, saying art can convey complex environmental messages in a 'visceral and engaging manner.'
Hector Mendez's installation 'Reverie of the Reef' used reclaimed ocean plastics to simulate a coral reef and prompt discussion on plastic overconsumption.
The 'Earth Rhythms' arts and crafts fair in Asheville, North Carolina on September 18 featured pottery with locally sourced clay and plant-based dyemaking workshops.
The 'Young Sprouts Artistic Jam' in Chicago on September 25 had young people make art from recycled materials; eight-year-old Lily Tran decorated a toy collection with scrap fabric.
London's 'Green Tides Festival' on October 7 showcased bio-degradable 3D printing filaments, solar-powered displays and Maya Ghali's hand-weaved tapestries of organic fibers.
The 'Voices of the Earth' festival in Santa Fe, New Mexico on October 14 featured indigenous artist Dakotah Soto, who paints with natural pigments sourced from the Earth.
The 'Eco Echo Art Parade' in Seattle on November 2 had participants parade in costumes made from upcycled materials.
The 'Sustainable Arte Fair' in Milan and the 'Eco Expression Expo' in Melbourne show the phenomenon extends beyond the United States.
The 'Artists for Earth' fund was established at New York's 'EcoVision Festival' on November 18 to support eco-art projects in public schools.
